passage: After the film society meeting in the student union in Gothenburg, Daniel caught Lars by the coat rack. "Hey, can I say something? The 'ask grandpa Daniel, he remembers the olden days' joke. You've made it three times now. It lands like I don't belong here." Lars felt his face heat up. He had been trying to include Daniel, who was thirty-four and back at university after years in a warehouse. "Come on, it's just banter. Everyone jokes." Then he stopped. Daniel wasn't laughing; he was just waiting. Lars took a breath. "Okay. I didn't mean it that way, but I get that it came across like that. Sorry. I'll drop it." "Thanks," Daniel said. Lars wanted to add that he wasn't a bad guy, that he'd only meant to be friendly. He zipped his coat instead and said, "See you Thursday."

qa.a: He had made it three times.

qa.q: What was the turning point in Lars's response, and why did it work?
qa.a: Seeing Daniel simply waiting made him stop defending himself; he apologised for how it landed and promised to drop it, without asking Daniel to reassure him.

qa.q: What might it have cost Daniel to raise this by the coat rack?
qa.a: Daniel risked seeming touchy with a younger group he is trying to fit into, so Lars's simple sorry probably came as a relief.

passage: In the electronics lab, during viva practice, Irfan was explaining the circuit slowly, getting stuck on a word as he sometimes did. Abhinav jumped in, grinning. "Resistor. Let me save us time, bro." A few people laughed. Irfan finished the sentence anyway and sat down. Later, while they packed up, Meghna came over. "Abhi, quietly: finishing his sentences like that isn't helping. It made him look slow in front of everyone." Abhinav's first thought was, I was just speeding things up. His second was, why is she making me the villain? His ears were burning. He wanted to argue. Instead he said, "I didn't see it like that. You're right, though." He found Irfan at the cycle stand. "Sorry about the viva thing. I won't do that again." Irfan shrugged. "Okay." Abhinav didn't ask if they were fine. He left it there.

qa.a: "Resistor."

passage:
Abhinav,
I'm writing this because I'm bad at saying things properly in person, and yesterday I proved it.
When you told me quietly after dinner that my "you'll make someone a great wife" line wasn't funny any more, my first reaction was to get annoyed. I said I was complimenting your biryani. I said you were being sensitive. Then I went back to my room feeling embarrassed and a bit hard done by, like you'd decided I was some kind of jerk.
I've thought about it since. It's the third or fourth time I've said something like that, and every time it turns your cooking into a joke instead of a skill. So I'm sorry for how it landed, not just sorry that you were upset. I'll stop.
You don't need to reply or tell me it's fine. Just make biryani again sometime. I'll wash up.
Yusuf

passage: You want the honest version, Ifeoma? Fine. I'm Manoj, and last month I found out I'd been that guy. In robotics club I had this habit with Gopika. Whenever we debugged, I'd say, "Okay, let me explain it simply," and slow right down, just for her. I thought I was being helpful. Then one evening she waited till everyone had left and said, very quietly, "When you do that, it comes across like you think I can't follow. I wrote half the motor code." My face went hot. My first words were, "That's not what I meant, you're taking it wrong." She just nodded and picked up her bag. I lay awake thinking, I'm not that guy, I'm nice. Next morning I found her by the lockers and said, "You're right. It came across badly, and I'm sorry." I didn't ask her to tell me it was fine. I've just stopped doing it.

qa.q: What did Manoj keep saying to Gopika while they debugged?
qa.a: "Okay, let me explain it simply."

qa.q: What was Manoj feeling right after Gopika spoke up?
qa.a: Manoj felt embarrassed and misjudged: the face went hot and the first words were "you're taking it wrong", because Manoj had believed the habit was helpful.

qa.a: Manoj stopped defending the intent, apologised for how it came across without asking Gopika for reassurance, and then dropped the habit, putting the effect ahead of Manoj's own comfort.

passage: I'm Wen, and I work the weekend shift at the campus café with Joseph and Zainab. For weeks, whenever Zainab was steaming milk with a serious face, Joseph would call across, "Smile! Customers like a smile!" and grin as if it were a bit between them. On Saturday, while I was wiping tables, Zainab stopped in the storeroom doorway and said something low to him. I only caught "every shift" and "I'm working, not sulking." Joseph's ears went red. He started, "I was only—" and for a second I thought he'd argue. Then he stopped and nodded. I heard, "Sorry. That came out wrong every time, then." He didn't hang about waiting for her to say it was okay. He went back to the till and served the queue. On Sunday he didn't say it once. He asked her how the new grinder worked instead.

qa.q: What did Joseph call across to Zainab during shifts?
